text_simplified: Parents must teach children the rights of Allah and the rights of parents from a young age. It is essential to instill religious and moral values in children's hearts gradually. Raising children upon *birr al-walidayn* (dutifulness to parents) and *ihsan* (excellence) is one of the most important duties of the family.

review_defects.english: birr al-walidayn (dutifulness to parents) and ihsan (excellence)
review_defects.why: The English adds 'al-walidayn' to 'birr', narrowing the meaning to dutifulness specifically to parents, whereas the Arabic 'البر' is general righteousness/dutifulness without specifying parents.
Arabic 'ينبغي' means 'should/ought', a softer recommendation; English 'essential' is stronger and more prescriptive, shifting the tone.
Arabic 'نفوس' means 'souls/self', while 'hearts' is a common but not exact rendering, slightly altering the intended depth.
